text.p: VALLETTA, Feb 17 Reuter - The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malta has highest population density in Europe, Council of Europe survey shows. There are 1,178 inhabitants per square kilometre, followed by San Marino with 411. The island also has the second lowest level of non-marital births among Council of Europe countries, coming second only to Cyprus.
- Teachers' union president calls for continual assessment system in schools to ease exams pressure on students.

- International Monetary Fund tells government not to remove VAT. An IMF team which visited Malta in January urged the new Labour government not to repeal value added tax, but was told that the government had an electoral mandate to do so. The government has refused to publish the IMF's recommendations.

- Local councils should insist on greater autonomy from the government, Opposition Leader Eddie Fenech Adami says. Fenech Adami is leading his party's campaign for local council elections due to be held in March in a third of Malta' towns and villages.

- Police investigate launch at Gozo. The launch, which drifted onto rocks in Gozo, Malta's sister island three miles to the north, was found to have no one on board, but it contained two life jackets and an empty fuel tank. There was some scribbling in Arabic.
- Prime minister says government planning the setting up of a regional council for Gozo.
